  "text": "The council fitted our street with lamps that showed tomorrow’s weather.

Blue meant rain. Amber meant sunshine. White meant snow.

On Tuesday, the lamp outside my house turned black.

Not unlit. Black. Its darkness pooled on the pavement, and passing dogs pulled their owners into the road.

I rang the number on the pole.

“Stay indoors tomorrow,” the woman said.

“What’s coming?”

She asked for my postcode, then went quiet.

“Is your mother still alive?”

“No.”

“Then don’t let her in.”

At nine the next morning, Mum knocked.

She wore the coat we’d buried her in, with the replacement button I’d sewn on crookedly. Through the letterbox came the smell of her hand cream.

“I’ve forgotten my key,” she said.

I sat on the stairs.

She knocked again.

“It’s freezing out here, love.”

Beyond the frosted glass, something fell steadily. It was too dark to be snow.

I called the council.

“Has she asked you to open the door?” the woman said.

“Yes.”

“And have you?”

“No.”

“Good. We’re sending someone.”

A van arrived at noon. Two men carried a ladder past Mum without looking at her. They replaced the lamp’s bulb.

Warm amber light spread across the street.

Mum was gone.

One of the men pushed a card through my letterbox.

FAULT RESOLVED. NO FURTHER ACTION REQUIRED.

I opened the door before they drove away.

“What was that?” I asked.

“Wrong forecast,” he said.

That evening, I found Mum’s crooked button on the step.

I was still holding it when every lamp along the street turned black."
